name: Kabuki brush

card.summary: A short-handled makeup brush with dense, rounded bristles that buffs loose or pressed powder, foundation and blush onto the face for an even, blended finish.

quick.overview:
A kabuki brush is a compact makeup brush with tightly packed bristles, usually rounded like a mushroom cap, though flat-topped versions exist. It is used to apply powder products such as foundation, face powder or blush across large areas of the face.

For appearance, the dense head lets makeup be pressed and buffed into the skin, which evens out tone and gives a smooth, natural-looking finish. The name comes from kabuki theatre, where actors used similar brushes to spread white rice powder.
quick.how: People use it to sweep, stipple or buff powder over the cheeks, forehead and jaw, or to blend foundation into the skin. Traditional versions used natural horse or goat hair, while most modern brushes use synthetic bristles. Angled and flat-top shapes are used for liquid foundation and fuller coverage.
quick.risks: There are no notable safety concerns beyond general hygiene: brushes can hold product and skin oils, so they need regular washing, as with any makeup tool.

lead: A kabuki brush, also called a mushroom brush, is a makeup brush with tightly packed bristles on a short handle. Its head is usually round, though flat versions exist [1]. It is used to apply loose powder products such as foundation, face powder or blush across large areas of the face, where its dense construction blends powder smoothly for a natural finish [1].

The name comes from kabuki, the traditional Japanese theatre form whose actors wear bold painted makeup; actors used these brushes to spread white rice powder evenly over their faces [1]. Traditional brushes used natural hair such as horse or goat, and most modern ones use synthetic bristles [1]. Wikipedia's makeup brush article describes flat-top and angled kabuki types as densely packed, and says they apply liquid foundation with full coverage [2].

chain: Dense bristles pick up and hold powder or foundation
Product is buffed into the skin in even layers
angle.text: The dense head spreads powder or foundation over broad areas of the face in an even layer. Users reach for it to mask shine, even out tone and blend makeup for a natural-looking finish.

paras: The brush has a compact grip and dense bristles, with a rounded head and occasionally a flat one [1]. Wikipedia's makeup brush article lists flat-top and angled versions [2].
The tool is named after kabuki theatre, whose performers applied white rice powder with such brushes [1]. The shift from natural hair to synthetic bristles is noted for modern products [1].

Today it is used for foundation, face powder and blush over large areas of the face, producing a blended finish [1]. The flat-top and angled variants are described as best suited to liquid foundation with full coverage [2].
